newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - October 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - October 24.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
FINANCIAL TIMES
-- MURDOCH SEEKS TO RAISE $1.5BN ON MARKETS

News Corporation, the media giant owned by Rupert Murdoch, is to go to the financial markets in a bid to raise about $1.5bn (960m stg). News Corp will issue preference shares which could be converted into British Sky Broadcasting shares. Prices are expected to be announced next week, along with final details about size and terms.
-- MGAM MAY LOSE PENSIONS CONTRACT WITH WESTMINSTER

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, the fund management company hit by a fraud inquiry into unit trust manager Peter Young, is facing the loss of a 200m stg mandate to manage pension funds for Westminster City Council. The Council is to invite tenders from other fund managers for the contract the manage half of its 400m stg pension fund.
-- CHELSEA DIRECTOR KILLED IN HELICOPTER CRASH

Millionaire businessman Matthew Harding, who was also vice chairman of Chelsea football club, has been killed in a helicopter crash as he returned from watching his team play in the north west. The 42-year old had a personal fortune estimated at 170m stg after building up one of the UK's largest reinsurance brokers. Earlier this year Harding made the headlines with the news he had donated 1m sterling to the Labour party.
-- CCA SET TO IMPOSE CUTS IN AIRPORT CHARGES

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), the regulator for the UK's airline industry, is expected to order airports operator BAA to make cuts of up to 100m stg over five years on landing and take-off charges at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports. The price controls are part of a regular five-yearly inquiry by the Authority into charges at airports.
-- BUSINESS GROUP'S CALL TO BACK EMU

The North East Chamber of Commerce, one of the largest in Britain, has launched a policy manifesto for the forthcoming general election which calls for a positive commitment from the UK to European economic and monetary union (Emu). The document claims that Emu will provide an environment of stability and discipline crucial to business success.
-- NATWEST OFFERS CHARGED ACCOUNT

High street retail bank National Westminster has followed the example of Barclays Bank and Royal Bank of Scotland by launching a fee-paying current account. The Advantage Premier account will carry an annual charge of 150 stg, and will offer a package of extras ranging from low overdraft rates to travel and theatre discounts. The move follows research which showed that people would be willing to pay for an account if they found it offered them enough additional features.
-- SHARES IN SAP PLUNGE ON WARNING

A warning on future sales and profit growth by the German business and software group SAP prompted a fall in its share price on the Frankfurt stock exchange of almost 25 per cent. The warnings accompanied the announcement of third quarter results, which saw SAP - one of the world's largest software companies - profits down to DM135m from DM152m.
-- POLYGRAM SEES FLAT ANNUAL RESULT

PolyGram, the world's largest music company, has issued a profits warning and announced it is to take a $90m reorganisation charge following lower-than-expected music sales. PolyGram said it expects full-year 1996 results before restructuring charges to be flat. The company had expected to see a rise in sales in the second half, traditionally a higher sales period, and as new albums were planned from some of the label's biggest stars. But Irish rock group U2 have delayed the launch of their new album until after the all-important Christmas period.
-- AT&T TO BE RUN BY NEWCOMER TO TELECOMS

US telecommunications giant AT&T has announced that John Walter, an executive who spent his working life at commercial printing company RR Donneley and who has no experience in the telecoms industry, will succeed Bob Allen as chief executive when he retires in 18 months' time. In the interim, Walter will become AT&T's number two executive with the titles of president and chief operating officer.
-- BA POISED TO GAIN CONTROL OF FRENCH CARRIER

British Airways look set to win control of the French carrier Air Liberte after threatened bids from Virgin Express and French commercial pilot Fernand Denan failed to materialise. If BA wins the bid it will be able to operate Air Liberte in tandem with TAT, its existing French airline, and in competition with Air France.
